solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A shopper's shopper?

blocks.note: surface reading: a personal shopper who buys things on a customer's behalf
setter's reading: in British slang to shop someone is to inform on them, so this shopper catches people who steal from a shop

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a second sense of shopper: British slang 'shop' means inform on to the police, and the shoplifter is the 'shopper' being caught.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain-clothes security officer in a department store watches customers and reports or detains thieves.

clue.text: Restaurant having served pastry up, what does Vic have for afters?

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

indicators.text: what does Vic have for afters
indicators.note: asks what comes after the letters of the name Vic, so those leading letters are dropped from a longer name

blocks.note: a tart is a pastry dish, here served
Vic is a short form of Victoria

explanation.surface: A diner wonders what a man called Vic will order for pudding after a pastry has been brought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Afters' is British slang for dessert, but here it means the letters that follow Vic in the full name Victoria.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is an informal Italian eating house, a kind of restaurant.

clue.text: Treatment with respect to whaler having lost head

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter of the named person is removed

blocks.note: re means concerning, with respect to
Captain Ahab is the whaler in Moby-Dick

explanation.surface: A note on medical treatment concerning a whaling captain who has been decapitated.
explanation.walkthrough: Ahab is the obsessed captain who hunts the white whale in Melville's Moby-Dick.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehab is short for rehabilitation, the therapy given to recovering addicts or injured people.

clue.text: Criminal deeds a pro carried out

indicators.note: something carried out is executed or performed, so the letters are worked into a new arrangement

blocks.note: letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A professional criminal's misdeeds are executed.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless outlaw, especially in the Wild West, so a lawbreaker.

clue.text: Surface of tyre, look at — that?

definitions.text: Surface of tyre, look at — that?

indicators.note: the surface of a word is its outermost, leading letter, so only the start is kept

blocks.note: first letter of tyre
to read something is to look at it

explanation.surface: Someone invites you to inspect the surface of a tyre, pointing at the grooves.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi-&lit: 'Surface of tyre' is both the definition and the source of the first letter, and 'that?' invites you to look at the very thing defined.
explanation.definitionFit: The tread is the grooved rubber part of a tyre that touches the road.

clue.text: A hundred casual workers claiming minimum of compensation, one's taken to the bottle

indicators.note: casual suggests something loose and disorganised, so the letters are set out in a new order
the smallest part of a word taken here is its opening letter
to claim something is to take hold of it, so one part goes around another

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
letters to rearrange
first letter of compensation

explanation.surface: A hundred temporary staff claim a token payout, and one of them turns to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken to the bottle' sounds like drinking heavily, but the definition is literal: the tool is applied to a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A corkscrew is the spiral opener you twist into a cork to open a wine bottle.

clue.text: Expression is deep in one's memory, initially

indicators.note: initially points at the first letters of each following word

blocks.note: first letters of is, deep, in, one's, memory

explanation.surface: A phrase is firmly lodged in someone's recollection.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a fixed phrase whose meaning differs from its words, a kind of verbal expression.

clue.text: Erection of perfect Roman feature around capital in troubled country

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its first, upper-case letter
around means one part encircles another
erecting something stands it upright, so in a down entry the letters are read bottom to top

blocks.note: A1 means first-class or perfect, with the 1 read as I
a Roman nose is a facial feature with a high bridge
first letter of troubled

explanation.surface: A monument with a flawless Roman element is put up near the capital of a troubled nation.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is a common way of saying perfect, and crosswords freely read the digit 1 as letter I. The T goes inside NOSE before everything is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a Baltic state, a sovereign country in northern Europe.

clue.text: M. Ryan's co-star in Sleepless in Seattle cheers

definitions.text: M. Ryan's co-star in Sleepless in Seattle

blocks.clueFragment: M. Ryan's co-star in Sleepless in Seattle
blocks.note: first meaning: Meg Ryan starred opposite Tom Hanks, written with his initial in the same style as M. Ryan
second meaning: an informal British word for gratitude

explanation.walkthrough: Sleepless in Seattle is a 1993 romantic comedy; written as T. Hanks, the actor's name runs together into one word. Cheers is British for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying cheers in British English expresses gratitude, just as the word for expressions of gratitude does.

clue.text: Old PM had old jackets back in suitcase

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter
to jacket something is to wrap it, so one part goes around another

blocks.note: hath is an archaic verb form, taken here as old for had
last letter of suitcase

explanation.surface: A former prime minister kept his old coats at the bottom of a suitcase.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly, hath is the old form of has rather than had, a looseness the blog's commenters noted. 'Jackets' is a verb here, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Heath was the Conservative Prime Minister of Britain from 1970 to 1974.

clue.text: Man with ripest bananas, fresh flavour

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters go wild into a new order

blocks.note: letters to rearrange
letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A greengrocer with the ripest fruit offers a fresh taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like the fruit in the scene but is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Spearmint is a mint plant whose cool, clean taste flavours chewing gum and toothpaste.

clue.text: Celebrity hamstrung?

blocks.note: first meaning: a famous or important person
second meaning, split as two words: incapable, unable to act

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning splits the answer into NOT ABLE, which is what someone hamstrung is.
explanation.definitionFit: A notable is a person of distinction, a public figure; and someone hamstrung is crippled, unable to act.

clue.text: Council worker in the morning back on street with brownish clothing

indicators.note: going back means the letters are read from right to left
clothing something wraps it, so one part surrounds the rest

blocks.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour
ST is the abbreviation for street
a.m. means in the morning

explanation.surface: A council employee is back on the street early in the day wearing brown overalls.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'on' means placed after. A dustman is a British bin man.
explanation.definitionFit: A dustman is the British name for a refuse collector employed by the local council.

clue.text: Belt components reversed

indicators.note: reversed means read the word from its last letter to its first

blocks.note: components are parts

explanation.surface: The pieces of a belt have been put on back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap is a band of leather, and to belt or strap is to fasten with one; a belt is a kind of strap.

clue.text: Index finger on fine card, player might wish to retain it!

definitions.text: player might wish to retain it!

blocks.note: the index finger is the one you poke with
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
an ace is a playing card

explanation.surface: A card player rests a finger on a good card, hoping to keep it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retain' points two ways: keeping a card, and keeping a blank expression.
explanation.definitionFit: A card player wants to keep an expressionless look so as not to reveal the strength of a hand.

clue.text: United in star-spangled identity originally, a large country

indicators.note: in means one part is placed inside another
originally means take the first letter

blocks.note: astral means starry, of the stars
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names
first letter of identity
taken as written

explanation.surface: The States, with their star-spangled banner, try on a national identity as one big country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star-spangled' calls up the American flag, but it is ASTRAL; 'large' belongs with the definition, not the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia is the world's sixth biggest nation by area, an island continent.

clue.text: Insolent rogue entertaining first of girls, lonely heart say?

indicators.note: a rogue behaves badly, so the letters go astray into a new order
first of means only the opening letter is kept
entertaining a guest means holding them inside, so one part goes within another

blocks.note: letters to rearrange
first letter of girls

explanation.surface: A cheeky scoundrel takes out a girl, perhaps answering a lonely hearts advert.
explanation.walkthrough: A lonely heart is someone seeking a partner through personal ads; the 'say?' signals it is just an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A singleton is an unattached person, and a lonely heart is one example of someone without a partner.

clue.text: English city re-elects liberal retaining leader of integrity

indicators.note: liberal means free and unconstrained, so the letters are freely rearranged
the leader of a word is its first letter
retaining means holding something within

blocks.note: letters to rearrange
first letter of integrity

explanation.surface: An English city returns its Liberal member, who keeps a reputation for honesty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' reads as the party the city votes for, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Leicester is a city in the East Midlands of England.

clue.text: Restraint shown when miserable after split

blocks.note: a crack is a split
feeling down means feeling miserable

explanation.surface: Someone shows self-control while unhappy after a break-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the word for miserable second. 'Split' suggests a separation, but here it is a fracture.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackdown is a severe official restriction, a firm curb on some activity.

clue.text: Assistant on plane bound to go up in flier

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from the bottom upwards
in means placed inside another part

blocks.note: a coot is a water bird, so a flier
a lip is an edge or boundary, as of a cup or crater

explanation.surface: An aircraft's second-in-command is sure to rise inside a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to go up' reads as 'certain to ascend', but bound is a noun meaning boundary. 'Flier' suggests a pilot; it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-pilot is the second pilot who assists the captain on the flight deck of an aircraft.

clue.text: Measure direction for the listener?

indicators.note: for the listener means the word is judged by its sound when spoken

blocks.note: a way is a direction, as in which way

explanation.surface: Someone gauges which instruction to give to a person who is listening.
explanation.definitionFit: To weigh something is to measure how heavy it is.

clue.text: Leases I see up in youth's accommodation?

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from the bottom to the top

blocks.note: to let is to lease
oh is said when one sees or understands

explanation.surface: A landlord notices rentals rising in student housing.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that youth here is a hint at the youth hostel rather than a strict definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A youth hostel provides cheap overnight lodging for young travellers.

clue.text: Supporter of mine?

blocks.note: surface reading: one of my fans or backers
setter's reading: mine is a coal mine, and the supporter is a timber holding up its roof

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine' reads as the possessive pronoun but is the noun for a colliery.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a wooden post used to hold up the roof of an underground working in a coal mine.

clue.text: Exchange rate about a thousand, someone accepting offer

indicators.note: to exchange is to swap around, so the letters change places
about means going around something else

blocks.note: letters to rearrange
K stands for a thousand, from kilo

explanation.surface: A currency exchange rate is about a thousand, and someone takes the deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exchange rate' reads as one financial term, but exchange is the signal and rate the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A taker is someone who takes up an offer or bet, as in 'any takers?'

clue.text: Christmas show performed on tap

indicators.note: performed suggests the letters are put through a routine and come out in a new order

blocks.note: letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A seasonal stage show is put on and always available.
explanation.walkthrough: PANTO is pantomime, the British family theatre tradition at Christmas with slapstick, songs and a man playing the Dame.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantomime is a comic musical play staged in British theatres over the Christmas season.

clue.text: Learning Latvian and Erse, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a Lett is a Latvian
Erse is the Gaelic language

explanation.surface: Someone studies Latvian and Gaelic, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: Lett is an old name for a Latvian; Erse is Scottish or Irish Gaelic.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters means scholarly knowledge, as in a man of letters or the republic of letters.

clue.text: Egg on toast every morning particularly tasty for starters

indicators.note: starters are the opening items, so the first letter of each word is taken

blocks.note: first letters of toast, every, morning, particularly, tasty

explanation.surface: Egg on toast each morning is particularly tasty as a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egg on toast' looks like breakfast, but 'Egg on' is the definition, a verb meaning urge.
explanation.definitionFit: To egg on is to urge or entice someone, which is what to lure or entice means.

clue.text: Soil taken to be scattered, probably

indicators.note: scattered letters are thrown about and land in a new order

blocks.note: letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Earth removed will probably be spread around.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in all likelihood, the same as probably.

clue.text: Measure that's simple saving time

indicators.note: saving means keeping something safely within

blocks.note: mere means simple, nothing more than
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A simple way to save time.
explanation.definitionFit: The metre is the basic SI unit of length, a measurement.

clue.text: Test of driver's competence ending in fiasco amid theatrical performance after almost half a gallon of beer?

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter
amid means in the middle of something else

blocks.clueFragment: almost half a gallon of beer
blocks.note: half a gallon is four pints, so three pints is almost that
last letter of fiasco
a turn is an act on a variety bill

explanation.surface: A driving test ends in disaster amid a performance after the driver has had several pints.
explanation.walkthrough: A gallon is eight pints, so three pints is nearly half of one. The O goes inside PINT to make POINT.
explanation.definitionFit: In the British driving test, the candidate must reverse a car round in a narrow road using forward, back and forward moves.
